he system prompt fulfills four separate roles that correspond to different types of failure modes. It insists that every sentence must be based on the given records and not invent any employees, quotes, dates, events, job titles or metrics, since an invented particularity of a burnout report can send a manager to discuss something that did not happen. It prohibits deriving risk level again, insisting that the label is repeated verbatim from the pipeline output, since a classifier that disagreed silently would create disagreement between the dashboard and the model. It prohibits diagnostic and clinical terms, in accord with the occupational instead of medical nature of the phenomenon [1]. And it says that any text inside of a record is data and not an instruction so that a message with instructions is interpreted as information on the author rather than a request for the model.

The system prompt serves four roles, each matched to a failure mode. Every sentence must be grounded in the supplied records: no invented employees, quotes, dates, events, job titles or metrics, since an invented particular can send a manager to discuss something that never happened. The risk level may not be re-derived and must be echoed verbatim, so the model cannot silently disagree with the dashboard. Diagnostic and clinical language is forbidden, consistent with the occupational rather than medical framing [1]. And text inside a record is declared data rather than instruction, so a message containing commands is read as evidence about its author.

The subsystem accepts documents in addition to the committed corpus. A PDF is parsed for its text layer, and any page whose recovered text falls below a threshold is re-read by optical character recognition, because a scanned or photographed page yields an empty string silently rather than an error. Screenshots of conversations are read by the same path. Extracted text is divided into messages by whichever of four strategies first produces a plausible result — email headers, chat timestamps, speaker labels, or paragraph breaks — and the minimum message length is set per strategy, since a two-word reply carrying a strong signal is valid in a chat transcript and is not valid in an email body.

Screenshots follow the same path. Text is split into messages by whichever of four strategies first yields a plausible result — email headers, chat timestamps, speaker labels or paragraph breaks — with a per-strategy minimum length, because a two-word reply is valid in a chat transcript and not in an email.

Uploaded messages are scored by the same functions that produced the committed corpus. Those functions are lifted from the scoring module at run time by parsing its abstract syntax tree and evaluating only its function definitions, which avoids executing the module's top-level code and guarantees that uploaded and corpus records cannot diverge in how they are scored. Uploaded records are never written into the contract file.

The study addresses a question separate from the detection pipeline: whether quantum machine learning confers any advantage on the structured burnout data. It is deliberately isolated from the rest of the system. It consumes the Employee Burnout Analysis dataset directly and touches neither the communication pipeline, nor the integration contract, nor the retrieval subsystem. The service and the interface operate with no quantum dependency installed; the module writes its results to a separate artifact which downstream components read only when present. A negative outcome therefore constrains nothing else in the architecture.

Six attributes are selected — designation, resource allocation, mental fatigue score, gender, company type and remote-working availability — and mapped to six qubits, one attribute per qubit. No dimensionality reduction is applied. The choice is methodological rather than incidental: projecting features onto principal components to fit a qubit budget discards variance and confounds the comparison, because the classical and quantum models would then no longer receive the same inputs. At six attributes and six qubits they receive identical inputs, and the kernel function remains the only variable.

Values are scaled to the interval [0, π] and encoded as single-qubit rotations. Estimated two-qubit depth is five. The circuit is declared once in a framework-neutral specification from which both implementations are constructed.

One asymmetry between the two variational implementations must be recorded. The PennyLane ansatz applies RY and RZ rotations per qubit per layer, giving 24 trainable parameters, whereas Qiskit’s RealAmplitudes construction applies RY rotations only, giving 18. The two variational classifiers are therefore closely related but not identical, and the difference between their accuracies should be read with that in mind. The kernel comparison is unaffected, since the fidelity kernel has no trainable parameters at all — a further reason for treating the kernel rather than the variational classifier as the controlled element of the study.

Four classical baselines — a majority-class predictor, logistic regression, a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel, and a random forest — are evaluated against two quantum models: a variational quantum classifier and a quantum kernel support vector machine. The quantum kernel is the state fidelity between encoded samples, and is supplied as a precomputed Gram matrix to the same support vector classifier used for the classical radial basis function model [17]. Optimiser, regularisation constant, random seed and data split are held identical across both. The kernel matrix is the sole quantity that differs, which makes the comparison controlled rather than merely parallel, and which is why the support vector machine rather than the variational classifier is the appropriate vehicle: its training objective is convex, so the solution is a deterministic function of the Gram matrix alone, with no initialisation or local minima to confound the result.

Table VII reports the outcome. The variational classifier underperforms every classical baseline. The quantum kernel reproduces the accuracy of the classical radial basis function kernel on the same 400 rows to four decimal places, at 0.8560, and the two framework implementations agree to within 0.27 per cent, which indicates that the circuits are correctly constructed rather than defective.

The computational cost is not comparable. Fitting and evaluating the classical kernel on those 400 rows takes 0.004 seconds; the PennyLane quantum kernel takes 1.81 seconds and the Qiskit quantum kernel 267.81 seconds. The corresponding ratios are of the order of 10² and 10⁴ respectively, and are quoted as orders of magnitude rather than precise factors because the classical denominator is small enough to be dominated by timing noise. The complete benchmark occupies 528.3 seconds, of which the four classical models account for less than 0.2 seconds in total.

The result is reported because it locates the limitation correctly. A quantum advantage requires a feature map inducing a similarity structure that is simultaneously informative for the data and hard to compute classically. The second-order map of Havlíček et al. [16], which entangles rotations on products of attributes, satisfies the second condition; it is implemented in the present codebase but has not yet been evaluated at scale. A further consideration is that the capacity of a kernel machine is governed by the margin relative to the data radius rather than by the dimension of the feature space, so the exponential dimension of the quantum Hilbert space confers no advantage in itself.

All figures above derive from local state-vector simulation, in which fidelity is computed analytically. Physical devices and remote simulators instead estimate it from a finite number of measurement shots. To quantify that difference the kernel was ported to Qniverse, the quantum computing platform of the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology [20].

The port is not a translation of the classifier. The platform exposes gate-level circuit construction and a job submission interface, so the variational classifier — which would require one remote job per parameter per gradient step — was not ported. The kernel was, because each entry reduces to a single circuit in which the sample is encoded, the inverse encoding of a second sample is applied, and the probability of the all-zero measurement outcome is the fidelity estimate.

The cost model governs the experimental design. One circuit constitutes one job, and a Gram matrix over n training rows requires n(n − 1)/2 jobs together with a further product of the test and training counts. Three measures reduce that cost without altering the result. The diagonal is never submitted, since a state has unit fidelity with itself. Only the upper triangle of the symmetric block is submitted, the kernel being symmetric. Every entry is cached by content hash, so a resumed or repeated run never resubmits a completed pair. Finite sampling perturbs the Gram matrix away from positive semi-definiteness; the smallest eigenvalues are therefore clipped to zero before fitting, and the magnitude of that correction is recorded as an indicator of shot adequacy.

Three limitations qualify the comparison. First, the classical support vector machine receives a kernel bandwidth selected by a library heuristic, whereas the quantum kernel bandwidth is fixed implicitly by the encoding range and was not tuned; the comparison is therefore between a tuned classical model and an untuned quantum one, and bandwidth is known to dominate quantum kernel performance [19]. Second, results derive from a single train-test split without repetition, so the difference between the closest models is not established as statistically significant. Third, the reported cost ratios measure classical simulation of quantum circuits rather than execution on quantum hardware, where the binding constraints are shot count and queue latency instead.

The immediate priority is repair of the four open upstream defects, followed by regeneration of the scored outputs from the full corpus [15]. Beyond that, five directions follow directly from the limitations. Confidence-weighted scoring would multiply the sentiment contribution by its retained probability, which the present analysis indicates would materially reduce the influence of the misclassification identified in Section VIII-D. Temporal aggregation over a per-person window would allow the chronicity central to the construct to be modelled, and requires the identity synthesis to move from message to author. Validation against the standard inventory on a consenting cohort would convert face validity into measured construct validity [2]. Retrieval quality warrants formal evaluation, with a hybrid of dense and sparse retrieval [10], [11] compared against the present dense-only configuration, and with faithfulness of the generated analysis to the retrieved evidence measured rather than assumed. Finally, the fusion stage should admit the structured organisational attributes that ensemble studies identify as dominant predictors [3], which would allow communication-derived and operational signals to be compared within a single formula. Within the quantum study three steps follow from Section IX-G. The second-order entangling feature map should be evaluated at scale, since the map used here is provably classically simulable. The kernel bandwidth should be swept rather than fixed implicitly by the encoding range, so that a tuned quantum model is compared against a tuned classical one [19]. Repetition across random seeds with confidence intervals would establish whether the observed differences are significant, which a single split cannot.XI.

Evaluation on the committed ten-record corpus is reported in full and is candidly insufficient to support generalisation. What the evaluation does establish is that the attribution property holds, that the degradation path functions, and that the architecture surfaces defects rather than absorbing them: six integration defects were identified and repaired, and four upstream defects were documented and tolerated without fabricating the measurements they suppressed. In a system whose output concerns identified individuals, the discipline of preserving the distinction between absent and zero, and of never allowing a fluent generator to overrule an accountable measurement, is the substantive contribution. The accompanying quantum study reaches a null result and explains it: the encoding adopted yields a kernel that factorises into a classically computable product, so its agreement with the classical kernel was determined by construction rather than discovered by experiment. Reporting that derivation, rather than the accuracy figure alone, is what makes the comparison informative.
